title: Jindal Drilling & Industries Ltd - 511034 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Jindal Drilling Q1 FY27: ONGC awarded a rig contract at ~INR45 lakh/day fixed; order book INR1,310 crore, with three rigs to dehire later in FY27.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as fairly good and broadly in line with expectations, with total revenue flat over the previous couple of quarters. EBITDA was stable; the variation in other expenses was driven by forex, which was more pronounced in Q4 FY26 and less so in Q1 FY27. The key development was a new ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer, which is under refurbishment in UAE with deployment targeted for October 2026. The order book stands at INR1,310 crore, and three rigs are expected to dehire within FY27, which management said will reduce H2 revenue. The call also disclosed a JV loss tied to Pioneer refurbishment and an update on a long-running ONGC legal dispute.

segments.name: Rig contracting (offshore jack-up)
segments.commentary: Five rigs on long-term ONGC contracts, with the sixth rig (Pioneer) newly contracted. Most EBITDA comes from owned rigs and rigs on good day rates. Fixed-rate contract for Pioneer at about INR45 lakh/day, INR-denominated, versus a bid of USD62,000/day that was pushed to about USD47,800/day.

guidance_outlook: Three rigs (Discovery-I, Virtue-I, Jindal Star) expected to dehire in later part of FY27; H2 FY27 revenue expected to decline, with EBITDA declining less than proportionally and margin possibly rising.
Blended EBITDA margin target of 35% reiterated as earlier guidance.
Post-dehire refurbishment of 4-6 months with no revenue; INR90-110 crore estimated refurbishment cost per rig.
Pioneer refurbishment expected to finish by first week of September 2026, with deployment in October 2026.
Company expects cash position to improve; no acquisitions planned, focus on redeploying the three dehiring rigs.
Discovery-I and Jindal Star contracts had a slight extension in duration (per presentation).
capex_capacity: Jindal Pioneer refurbishment carried out in UAE through a joint venture; spend not disclosed. Completion by first week of September 2026 and deployment in October 2026.
Three rigs dehiring in later FY27 will need 4-6 months refurbishment each, at an estimated INR90-110 crore per rig.
Company acquired one rig in FY25 and refurbished it; cash conserved for upcoming refurbishments.
Tenders must be submitted separately for each rig owned, though multi-rig tenders are possible.
demand_pricing: Pioneer contract awarded at fixed INR45 lakh/day (approx.), INR-denominated; management said the rate was pushed down from its USD62,000/day bid to about USD47,800/day.

Redeployment of dehired rigs has been difficult for all drillers over the past two years; management expects the three dehiring rigs to be re-hired, citing the Government of India's Samudra Manthan exercise.
Day rates for the next three rigs expected to improve, though management declined to guide on rates; order book shows wide day-rate variation.
Focus is domestic (ONGC); international deployment considered only if opportunities arise, given existing-participant preference and counterparty and country risk.
Management could not say how many competing rigs are available in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Likelihood, timing and rates for renewal of the three rigs expiring in 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: After dehire there is a 4-6 month refurbishment with no revenue. Redeployment is fairly likely, though subject to tender nuances; management declined to comment on rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 FY27 revenue fall materially with three of six rigs out of contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, revenue will decline in H2. EBITDA is expected to decline less than revenue because the dehiring rigs include Discovery-I (owned), Virtue-I and Jindal Star, and the decline in earnings comes mainly from two rigs; margin may rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR denomination of the new contract fixed, and will INR or USD apply going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed day rate of about INR45 lakh, INR-denominated. Management will update on whether future tenders are in USD or INR next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a loss in the JV, and will it return to profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV was the seller of Pioneer and is funding refurbishment to bring the rig to contracted condition, which is causing the loss in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisitions planned given improved cash and lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: No acquisitions planned. Focus is on redeploying three dehiring rigs, and cash is needed for refurbishments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ONGC dispute status and potential exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: No material update; the case has run 14-15 years and is in Supreme Court on appeal by ONGC. Company has received funds; if it loses (considered remote), it would repay about INR163 crore (INR63 crore USD receivable plus interest and forex).

risks_watch: Three rigs dehiring in later FY27 with 4-6 months of no revenue each; H2 FY27 revenue to decline.
Redeployment uncertainty: industry has struggled to re-hire rigs for two years; tender-based award process for each rig.
Pricing pressure: Pioneer bid cut from USD62,000 to about USD47,800/day; rate on renewals not guided.
Refurbishment capex of INR90-110 crore per rig may pressure cash; company says cash will improve.
ONGC legal dispute unresolved after 14-15 years; exposure about INR163 crore if lost (considered remote).
JV loss from Pioneer refurbishment; expected to be temporary per management's refurbishment explanation.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic. Management was confident on the Pioneer award and on redeploying the three dehiring rigs, but was evasive on rates, rig counts, the INR/USD denomination of future tenders, and the legal dispute, deferring those to later calls.

adds.what: Jindal Pioneer jack-up rig returning from UAE refurbishment, deployed on ONGC contract (sixth rig)

growth.why: Management guided H2 FY27 revenue to decline as three rigs dehire, with 4-6 months refurbishment at INR90-110 crore per rig and no revenue meanwhile; the Pioneer rig (INR45 lakh/day fixed, ONGC) returns in October 2026 and the 35% blended EBITDA margin target was reiterated, but no revenue growth figure or Q1 revenue/EBITDA numbers were stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said H2 FY27 EBITDA will decline less than revenue as three rigs dehire, so margin may rise, and the 35% blended EBITDA margin target was reiterated; but no Q1 EBITDA figure was stated and the Pioneer contract was won at INR45 lakh/day, down from a USD62,000/day bid cut to about USD47,800/day.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pioneer, the sixth rig, finishes refurbishment in UAE by the first week of September 2026 and deploys in October 2026 on a fixed INR45 lakh/day ONGC contract; however, three of the existing six rigs dehire in later FY27 and need 4-6 months refurbishment each at INR90-110 crore, so net fleet availability falls in H2.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Rig-days fall in H2 FY27 as three rigs dehire, with 4-6 months of refurbishment per rig, only partly offset by Pioneer deploying in October 2026; no volume growth figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three rigs need INR90-110 crore refurbishment each after dehire, but the company says cash is conserved for these refurbishments and no acquisitions are planned, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 revenue to decline as three of six rigs dehire with 4-6 months of no revenue each, and Pioneer was won at a cut rate, so a guidance raise is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Three rigs (Discovery-I, Virtue-I, Jindal Star) dehire in later FY27 and H2 FY27 revenue is guided lower; redeployment is uncertain given the industry has struggled to re-hire rigs for two years and day rates for renewals were not guided.

rows.label: Order book INR1,310 crore with Pioneer ONGC award
rows.why: Order book stands at INR1,310 crore and Pioneer is firmly contracted with ONGC at about INR45 lakh/day fixed, deploying October 2026.

rows.label: International deployment for rigs
rows.why: Focus is domestic on ONGC; international work considered only if opportunities arise, given existing-participant preference and counterparty and country risk.

rows.label: ONGC legal dispute exposure about INR163 crore
rows.why: Case has run 14-15 years and is at Supreme Court on ONGC's appeal; the company has received funds, and a loss (considered remote) would mean repaying about INR163 crore incl. interest and forex.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Pioneer award, deployment in October 2026 and redeploying the three dehiring rigs, but was evasive on day rates, rig counts, INR/USD denomination of future tenders and the ONGC dispute; analysts pressed on H2 revenue decline and the JV loss.
